Development guide

Tech Scan: Coding agents and coordination

Choose where a developer works, how the coding agent reaches a model and, when necessary, who coordinates several agents.

Draft research reference: vendor documentation, not locally deployed or benchmarked. Availability is not evidence that a configuration meets your organisation’s needs.

On this page
Decision gates Agents and model routes Coordination Controls and pilot Do not start on retired products Gaps and open questions Sources

Start with the decision gates

A coding agent can read a task, propose changes and use permitted tools. An editor is the developer’s interface; the agent may run in that editor, a terminal or a remote service. The model generates responses; the host runs the agent and its tools. Choosing one does not settle the others.

This scan starts with AWS hosting and managed Claude or OpenAI models through Amazon Bedrock. Treat direct provider APIs or another managed service as exceptions to assess, not as interchangeable Bedrock routes. These are scan assumptions, not newly established organisational policy.

  1. Capability: identify the task, editor, tool actions and features required on the exact route.
  2. Data: compare code sensitivity, processing geography, storage, retention and contractual terms against the approved requirements.
  3. Identity and authorisation: check user access, model access, repository permissions and service roles.
  4. Boundary: identify the agent host, execution environment, network egress, secrets and model endpoint, including fallback destinations.
  5. Ownership: name an operator, support and cost owner; establish monitoring, update, incident and exit arrangements.

The engineering lead records the version, configuration, evidence and unresolved conditions with the decision owner. A failed required gate rules out that configuration, even if it is AWS-first; obtain the applicable exception before evaluating a different route with real data.

Choose the agent and its model route

For a team already working in a terminal or supported editor, compare Claude Code and Codex with Bedrock as starting candidates. Kiro is another AWS-first candidate when its experience and governance satisfy the gates. Select a route for a representative task rather than declaring a universal winner.

Document the product, host and endpoint separately
Candidate and triggerRoute and material limit
Claude Code on BedrockUse the documented Bedrock configuration for Claude models; identify Invoke API or Mantle, model ID and region. Claude Code’s Bedrock route does not provide its web search or subscription-dependent cloud sessions; confirm the feature table for the selected workflow.[1][2]
Codex on BedrockOpenAI documents local Codex workflows on Bedrock. Codex cloud is not available on that configuration. Runtime and Mantle differ. Runtime is the bedrock-runtime endpoint and takes inference-profile IDs such as us. or global. prefixes; Mantle is the native OpenAI API shape at bedrock-mantle.<region>.api.aws/openai/v1 and takes openai. model IDs. Mantle is the Codex CLI's native path; OpenAI recommends Runtime for new configurations. In the Responses API, hosted web search and background mode are not available on Runtime; on Mantle, hosted web search is available on supported models and background mode is available only when the effective retention mode is not none. Setting store: false does not guarantee zero data retention. An AWS Region is not an OpenAI data residency jurisdiction: check the inference profile's destination regions, not only the endpoint URL. GPT-5.6 Sol or Terra is the current recommended tier; GPT-6 Sol, Luna and Astra are listed in OpenAI's documentation (November 2026), so verify the region and model ID at rollout. Check whether the client exposes the API feature you need.[3][4]
KiroConsider its editor or CLI when its workflow fits. Kiro documents Bedrock-backed cross-region inference and a choice beyond Claude and OpenAI.[11] Enable model access management and select approved named models.[5][6] Kiro says Auto can route to active models outside the approved list; exclude Auto when exact model choice is required, and test enforcement and inference geography in the intended enterprise configuration. Auto does not route to Experimental models, but it can route to open-weight models such as Grok 4.7, Kimi K3, MiniMax, DeepSeek and Qwen, which is why the block matters for a Bedrock-only policy. Fable 5.1 is US East only and Enterprise only, with all traffic retained up to 30 days.[12]

Two Bedrock endpoints serve Claude Code. The Invoke API takes a model ID or inference-profile ID; Mantle serves Claude models through the native Anthropic API shape and takes an anthropic. model ID with no version suffix, such as anthropic.claude-sonnet-5. Mantle has its own IAM actions under the bedrock-mantle: prefix (CreateInference, CountTokens); granting only bedrock:* does not cover it. Both endpoints can run in one session. Set CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1 for the Invoke API and CLAUDE_CODE_USE_MANTLE=1 for Mantle. Pin the model with the documented defaults: Opus 5.5 for the primary model and Sonnet 4.5 for smaller, faster work.[1]

Kiro local command boundary: Kiro says its local command sandbox is off by default. When enabled, it limits shell commands and their child processes; built-in file tools and remote HTTP and SSE MCP servers remain outside, while stdio MCP servers can be wrapped optionally. If the platform backend is unavailable, commands can run without operating-system isolation unless the current mode requires protection. Check sandbox status and all tool boundaries in the intended configuration; sandboxing is not a guarantee of isolation.[20]

Conditional editor alternative: Zed is worth assessing when the team needs a separate editor with external coding agents. Zed documents both Amazon Bedrock as a gateway and external agents, but the latter usually own their own authentication and model configuration. Zed's own agent uses Zed-configured models, including the Bedrock gateway. External agents — Claude, Codex, Copilot, Cursor, OpenCode, Gemini CLI and Pi, through the Agent Client Protocol — keep their own authentication, model configuration, subscriptions, tools, instructions and MCP configuration. Verify each agent’s actual route, identity and data terms; choosing an editor does not force every agent through Bedrock.[7]

For every candidate record the endpoint, model or inference profile, region and potential cross-region processing. Check the data path for prompts, repository contents, logs and external tools separately. Do not assume a gateway or fallback stays within the approved boundary; inspect every destination and disable or obtain approval for direct-provider paths. See Models and AI gateway.

Start with one agent; coordinate only when needed

Start with a single agent and a bounded task. A developer reviews its diff and test evidence. Add agents only if a task has separable work or a distinct expertise and the handoff is worth its extra cost, delay and failure modes. Starting with one agent is a working heuristic, not a vendor rule: one agent's failure modes stay visible before coordination multiplies them.

For example, a coding agent changes a function and a specialist independently checks tests. The supervisor passes the task and relevant evidence, collects the result and returns the diff to the developer. The specialist’s answer is not proof of correctness or authority to merge.

  • Supervisor and specialists: a supervisor calls a specialist as a tool and receives its result. Strands documents this pattern as agents as tools under a supervisor; assess it first when central control and bounded delegation suffice.[8]
  • Graph: use explicit nodes and edges when the task needs defined branches, dependencies or review stops. In Strands, a graph is a developer flowchart with a language-model decision at each node and shared state; state which conditions are model-driven and which are defined in code. LangGraph offers stateful graph orchestration for the same shape when the workflow needs durable state. Test persistence and recovery in the chosen deployment rather than assuming them.[8][9]
  • Fixed workflow: use a fixed sequence of steps with no cycles when the route is fully defined in advance. In Strands, a workflow is a fixed sequence of steps with no cycles (a directed acyclic graph) and parallel independent tasks. Use it when the steps, order and review stops do not change between runs.[8]
  • Peer handoffs: a swarm can let specialists choose the next agent; investigate it only if that flexibility is needed and the team can bound and audit the route. Name the product: Strands Swarm and LangGraph Swarm are peer-handoff frameworks, while OpenAI Swarm is an archived educational library superseded by the OpenAI Agents SDK; do not start new work on it (see Do not start on retired products).[8]

Set delegation limits, timeouts, budgets and a failure route; record task inputs, handoffs, tool calls and outcomes without exposing secrets. A human reviews changes before merge and the existing release authority remains separate. For one agent’s loop, tools and memory see Harness; for code execution boundaries see Sandbox.

Control access and run a pilot

Repository files, fetched pages, tool output and agent instructions can contain hostile instructions. Treat them as untrusted data. Use a scoped identity, least-privilege repository and cloud permissions, restricted outbound access and an isolated execution environment. Review instructions, hooks and tool servers before enabling them; protect the agent’s own permissions and trust configuration from unauthorised edits. Avoid blanket approval of shell commands and never put secrets in prompts or commands. Anthropic’s security guidance describes prompt-injection and permission risks for Claude Code; the exact controls differ by product.[10]

Enforce two rules before any pilot. First, no agent writes its own trust configuration: mcp.json, .vscode/tasks.json, .claude/settings.json and hook definitions stay under human control, because a crafted instruction can turn a write into code execution. Kiro CVE-2026-10591 is that failure: insufficient access control in the file-write tool before Kiro IDE 0.11 let crafted instructions write to execution-sensitive paths; upgrade to Kiro IDE 0.11 or later.[19] Second, no secrets in commands, prompts or allow-rules: a secret written into an agent's local configuration has leaked publicly in at least one November 2026 report, and a leaked allow-rule is a standing permission.[18]

Tibo (@thsottiaux) highlights approval fatigue when discussing OpenAI Auto-review.[21] Automated review is not an isolation boundary: retain independently enforced permission and network restrictions.

For a pilot, the engineering lead selects the same representative change and acceptance tests for each candidate, with non-sensitive data and an approved sandbox. Record task completion, human correction, elapsed time, cost, permissions, route and failure recovery. Attempt a denied action and confirm it is denied; inspect logs and outbound destinations. The decision owner compares the results with the gates, records gaps and either authorises a wider trial under the applicable process or stops. No local pilot, security test or comparison has been performed for this page.

Before adoption, confirm current feature availability, model IDs, retention and regional processing with the providers and your agreement. Product documentation is evidence of a stated capability, not local performance, compliance or a guarantee against prompt injection.

Do not start on retired products

Do not start new work on a product whose vendor has ended support. Use the replacement named in each row.

Gaps and open questions

The pinned defaults above are current for 13 November 2026. Confirm the current model IDs, regions and data terms with the provider before adoption, and re-check after re:Invent (29 November–4 December 2026), when AgentCore availability may change.

The orchestrator table covers Strands and LangGraph in depth; the other frameworks are summarised from the research proposal and need a direct comparison before adoption.[18]

Kiro Web is the closest managed factory option; it is assessed as a factory in Workflows & factories, not as an agent route here.
